author: Doctor
text:
Mel, all trades are taken with at least the 4hr chart in mind where possible. I want to have the minimum time frame with me when London opens. There are times when a setup comes after the first 4r period has elapsed after the London open. A pull back into the origin is common for my entries, at times I will take them early and scale in as the setup gets more orders in the market. Once I like what I see there is no hesitation and enter on the next closed candle. Pro money rarely gives a second shot an entry. If you have doubts, dont take it.

My check list is all mental these days, but in the early days I did have a checklist taped to my monitors. My journal is my trading posted into excel. Anyone starting off is wise to jot down all trades and any losers need careful analysis to see why it failed. There are trades which will fail even with the perfect setup, there is no such thing as a sure thing in trading.

Always maintain the longer time frames in your mind and know where each one is in the cycle.

This is the basis of being properly prepared.

Les_p, pro money wont do the same thing twice. They will do all possible to hide their movements and only show their true intentions after false moves and pain for the retail trader. This is the single most difficult part to figure out in trading. The changes only have a few set 'shapes' people look for, such as long wicks and tails. Some trade what they call pin bars only and design trading systems around them, but this is only a tiny part of the puzzle. The only way to see what pro money is doing is to spend a lot of time looking at charts. Good formations from candles form around support and resistance areas, which turn into supply and demand.

Castus, I dont place much emphasis on correlations because these will change over time and you cannot put much importance into them. At the moment look at the S&P500 and the AUD, over the past few months both are diverging. In my view too many traders look at too many other factors which are meant to have influence on a certain pair. I trade what I see on the chart of the pair I am interested, no external factors influence me unless price is at an important area and major news is due. Trading at a time like that will result in the price movement we saw last Friday in eur/usd which messed up a nice long setup and drove price down on nothing but emotion and the overwhelming new supply will have given pro money a lot of pain. There are times when the pro's cant hold an area.

author: Doctor
text:
blacky, the german open often pushes prices into false breaks and the London open an hour later reverses it. The majority of the worlds finance is traded through London and it makes sense to trade in that session. I dont trade the Yen or AUD very often, but if I do take it then its on the London session. Last year I may have taken a trade during the Asian session perhaps 4 or 5 times. Practically all trades are done in the London session.

Risk reward is highly individualistic. I trade between supply and demand and only adjust if I see the move weakening. I have no interest in risk reward in the typical fashion most see it. I trade for the major portion of a move and not become blinded with needing a risk reward. If risk reward is used, then it becomes an indicator and by now you will know my opinion on indicators. Position sizing has a huge effect on how far you wish to take the move and how long you stay in it. I can load up heavy and take the nearest support or resistance area as a target, or hold longer and look for the full move. If I am unwilling to wait for the entire move to end, I will have larger position sizes and hold them for a shorter period of time. My stop while I watch the trade is mental, and I use a hard stop when away from my trading station. As yet I am unable to stay awake for 24hrs and trade all the markets:)

And to take your first question last. When I started I wrote down trades and this was a bad way to keep track. You need to take screen shots of all time frames when you enter and mark them up where the entry, stop and target is. Along with that you type out the reasons why you took that trade. Trading is a visual thing and numbers wont help in getting the full story across. You need visual input. using more than one monitor is also essential in my view. As your trading evolves a pattern of what will eventually turn into a method will develop from your efforts. We are all different and learn at different speeds and in different ways. Dont take my way and the only way or best way. It is one of many ways. But there are principles to my trading that is applicable to all tastes. Take what you can from it and build upon it.

author: Doctor
text:
Castus, I was not born with trading in my blood and had to learn it the hard way. I have had exposure to pro traders and the world around it. I spent many many hours taking apart the maths behind just about every indicator ever made and know what makes them tick, and a lot of the people who invented them too. Lets just say, there is a cash cow that is created when a person gets a indicator made after them. Other than that, I see no benefit in any indicator and price itself is the only indicator I need.

You will be surprised to hear that if you were to talk to a pro trader, they will find it difficult to describe to you what they did in taking the last trade. All have different opinions and its more of a feel thing to a lot of them. I broke down trades to hard facts and built up a road map of all I could see. The result is what you see here on posted charts. The markets are based on certainty, price will go between two other price areas. This will never change.

Learn with your eyes and an analytic brain, it works and costs nothing but time.

author: Doctor
text:
blacky, there was a lot of news out of Europe last Friday and this was used by pro money to send price down to the last area of demand, but it fell so so hard that the wall of retail sellers and opportunistic bears means is not always possible to hold price back by the bulls and it means the pro money had to adjust positions and the tracks are all over the chart. Pro money has to soak up all selling orders if they want price to hold, but not all pro money will hold at the same area and they start a war between each other to see who can inflict as much pain on the other side and take out their limits. Times such as last Friday are opposing firms at work and when areas fail that we expect to have held start to fall through near term support. Opportunistic bears will also have seen this and taken shorter term orders to push it down to areas they want i.e the type who were holding draw down when the bullish move originally came. There is more than just bulls in the market and when price comes close to old areas where somebody got it wrong, they can hold and pounce later on.

Pro money will have hedged and others lightened up on positions. Pro money does not always win and their losses are based on their capital reserves which allow them hold through the draw down if they are big enough. Some can hold on for weeks or months if its viable and if the reserve funds are available for such times. Each firm will have their own rules internally. If the invested funds are from private investors, the call of what to do comes from the investor and not the firm.

High frequency trading is totally different to the way humans trade and you will not spot it unless you have inside knowledge of how it works. And the how it works is a closely guarded secret of the software algorithm. Each firm has their own and they protect this closely because the cost to produce it costs a hefty price tag. High frequency trading by nature is in and out fast, it will not cause price to drop or rise so dramatically.

Once you look back on the chart you can see the news was the reason for the price drop and as it was unable to hold levels, price was only going in one direction and will continue until the bulls either see value, or the bears pull it lower to their price area. A lot of traders will have been burned badly and the market has to settle from the big shake out. But that is trading, there is no defined set of rules where price will reach in a given time, other than it will get there eventually with all the twists and turns it takes.

There are two seasons in trading and it holds true for forex and stocks. In December postions for major players close early. I mentioned this last year and mid December is the time when most close out. It is a big time of the year for all banks and firms. In spring there tends to be a lot of volume placed in the market by longer term traders. This is mostly applicable to stock traders. Some traders are of the old guard where the start of the trading year is spring time and not January. In mid December I am closed out fully. If I happen to see a setup after that it will be short lived and wont push my luck, the volume tends to be gone and hitting a target is harder. Currencies are far more liquid than stocks and more opportunities to trade all year round.

IF, I got what you need. Listen to your Doctor.

It has been one of those days when the nearest news man would have been throttled had I been near one. Here is a chart of the eur/jpy. Even the beginners among can clearly see whats going on. But ask yourself, what did the media report/pimp?

The Euro has risen against the Yen (and other currencies). Yes by all means state the obvious, but why constantly since markets began have they got to plant the idea in your mind that this thing is taking off, when clearly it is into a major weekly area of supply. It is also a strong resistance area. The answer friends is a simple one, when pro money want to get to the next level and need a helping hand, their paid friends in the media do their 'bidding'. I use that word with a great deal of cheek.

The time is not right to buy eur/jpy, it is time if anything for a healthy pull back and watch the pro's take their large 2000+ point profit. Above current price is a real mess with choppy price action to the left. At the very least we need to push above the purple line and come back to test it holds. Then perhaps in a few weeks we will have either a bullish or bearish trade depending on what pro money decides.

Keep in mind if the euro is now being pimped long, pro money are either already in, or waiting to give it a false push and reverse. Watch key areas closely before you part with cash.

On a different topic. I did grab a few templates from yesterdays session you had with IF. Some of you have drafted very good charts with sensible areas marked. text:
Hello Doc, there are the entries opportunies i spotted today on EU.

Daily chart. Two obvious S&R. Last week, pro money made a strong shake out, pushed price consolidate into the original source of lastest up trend--- daily demand zone for several days. Yesterday, daily bar formed a bullish engulf bar to the former bar, give us some clue that pro money scaling into long now.

H4. I add a blue minor S&R on the chart. Its easy to see price consolidate within a range for long time. The wicks and tails reveal a intense conflict among pro moneys.

M15. Spot the entries. 1st entry can be opened after london session begins. Price rejected at the demand zone, formed long tails. Evey bars closed above the daily Suppot line, big clue. 2nd entry: after price breaks up the consolidated range, olde supply becomes new demand, daily resistence becomes support. When price first pullback, formed nice long tails closed above daily support line, showing pro money buys again. There's a green bar with long tail and wick, consume both retail traders' buy/sell orders. It helps to add fuel for pro for the next pushing up. Also, the 2nd entry opportunity occurs right after NY session starts.

If there's another chance to enter long today, i'll expect that price breaks up the upper daily S&R line and we can trade the pullback. It depends on whats NY boys'plan.

H4, target. The 1st target is beiing hitted now at the upper daily S&R. The 2nd target is the next level supply zone marked with green color. I will not supprise pro money will shake out again before price touch that level.

Compare with these maked entries: entry 1st provides the best RR, entry 2nd is more safefy and certainty.

Looking forward ur comment.

author: Doctor
text:
A brief reply and I am caught up in a few non trading days at the moment.

Your second entry was the only logical place to go long. The first entry was nothing but price leaving the bottom of a narrow price range and could at any time have fallen through the range and the momentum caused by stops being taken and new short orders come in cost you a lot of money. It is better to wait for price to break through the range in the original direction favored by pro money and wait for it to come back down to the origin and then look for an entry with price action. For price to fall back inside the range it means no interested buyers where we would expect to see support/demand. That is about as pure price action and candle reading as it gets. Others will take it on a candle close and not wait for price action. You need more capital for the entry on close alone.

I have not been in front of any charts for the past two days and have no idea where the euro is at present and cant comment further.

I find risk vs reward to be a misused and understood term. Pro money will go for open space between current price and an obvious target. It wont be based on risk vs reward but purely on enough room for price to move where it enables them to get their orders into the market. If you think logically about this it makes sense, you want to be where pro money is active and not scalping between 5 or 15min price areas. Of course this is considering you are willing to hold. The spread will be the same no matter how you trade but the profit is better when running with an active market. An example of holding in a trade over a day or two was my average 66 point stop last year on the euro. I was willing to take that based on an average 800 point win. Small change in the greater picture. For day trading the pull backs below the 1hr chart will be places to look for continuation. As you drop below the 1hr time frame the targets become much smaller and the false moves can then become a higher percentage of potential profit and risk reward then is of little benefit as it is a more scalpers scene. Taking trades in the same direction as pro money on lower time frames is possible but the pull backs are where it takes out a lot of day traders.

It is counter intuitive to go long in a falling market, but if this is done into support and with price action on your side and timing is correct i.e major market is open and at least the 4hr chart is also at support you can expect to see some action. The only unknown then is if a news release is due and its effect. But I think its being said enough times to wait until the ripples from the news have gone past their sell by date. And usually selling covertly planted cerebral non truths. That is about as nice I can be with the media today.

Your target for the second entry is ideal.

text:
Hello Doc, happy Valentine's day, hope u and ur family have a wonderful time.:)

Then, its another follow up of EU.

Daily. As expect, yesterday's daily candle forms a long wick, hanging on the lower edge of suppy zone. My plan is that if there's bearish moves following through in Asian or/and early London session, EU can be shorted. Otherwise, there might be a deep spike into the supply. So we should wait and hold our bias until london opens.

H4. There're some earilest sign for the bear move on h4 chart yesterday. First one is the strong red engulf candle, closed below the daily S&R of 1.3470.
